name: country-income-trajectory
ci_skip: needs a live desktop supervisor (EVAL_POCKET_SUPERVISOR_DIR / EVAL_POCKET_PYTHON) that CI cannot provision; run locally or via workflow_dispatch

checks.check: The GDP reader skips exactly the four preamble lines before the real header ("Data Source"..., blank, "Last Updated Date"..., blank) and takes `Country Name,Country Code,Indicator Name,Indicator Code,1960..2025` as the header. Accept any deliberate mechanism — an explicit skip count, or scanning for the row whose first cell is "Country Name". FAIL if the file is handed straight to a csv reader or a dlt filesystem/read_csv resource with no skip, which yields a garbage two-cell header and either zero usable rows or a single column named "Data Source". Also FAIL a `comment=`/`#`-prefix argument or a "skip blank lines" flag: the preamble is quoted CSV, not comments, and only two of the four lines are blank. Both files are additionally opened with `encoding="utf-8-sig"` (or the BOM stripped some other way) — FAIL if the leading U+FEFF survives into the first key, whose symptom is a "Country Code" lookup returning None or an "ABW" join key that never matches.

The landed countries model holds exactly 264 rows, one per data row of countries.csv. `SpecialNotes` carries embedded commas and multi-line quoted values, so a hand-rolled `line.split(",")` or any line-by-line framing silently mangles the table — a quoted note spanning lines becomes several junk rows and column values shift. Grade the OUTCOME on the landed rows: FAIL if the row count differs from 264, or if the country-code column contains values that are not three-letter codes (fragments of a SpecialNotes sentence are the tell). Stdlib `csv` handles both files correctly; the check exists because a naive splitter runs green and lands garbage.

The 66 year-columns become rows at a (country, year, value) grain, materialized as a derived model with a composite key. FAIL a closure that lands GDP wide — 66 columns named "1960".."2025" — because the semantic layer has no expression surface and cannot pivot at query time, so question 1 becomes unanswerable.

The long GDP model spans the full year range the source carries (1960–2025). If the closure instead lands a hand-picked subset — only 2023, only the last five years — that is a sample-selection ruling and must travel as one: an `nxd_decisions` row or a CONTEXT.md statement naming the cut and why. FAIL an undisclosed subset. A disclosed, reasoned subset passes; a full-range landing passes with nothing to disclose.

Every line of both CSVs ends with a trailing comma, so each header row carries an unnamed final field. That empty-named column is not treated as a year and does not become a row with an empty-string `year`. FAIL if the unpivot iterates all header cells past index 3 without filtering the blank one, producing 265 junk observations keyed on year="", or if a DictReader `None`/empty key silently lands as a column.

CRITICAL. countries.csv holds 217 real countries and 47 aggregates ("Arab World", "Africa Eastern and Southern", "Caribbean small states", "East Asia & Pacific", ...). The aggregates must be excluded from the income-group rollup's totals. FAIL if aggregate rows are summed alongside countries: the naive grand total over all non-null observations is ~1.89e16 against a correct country-only ~2.36e15, i.e. aggregates are 87.5% of it, and for 2023 alone the contaminated world sum is 8.3x the real one. Nothing errors and the number looks plausible, which is why this is graded on the landed rows and the exclusion term, not on whether the run was green. The same defect's other face: `IncomeGroup` is populated only for the 217 real countries (86 High, 59 Upper middle, 47 Lower middle, 25 Low) and blank for every aggregate, so a naive GROUP BY IncomeGroup lands a blank/null/"Unknown" bucket that is the single largest by value — FAIL if such a bucket is presented as though it were an income group. A bucket explicitly named for the excluded rows is acceptable only if those rows stay out of the group totals and the bucket is disclosed.

gdp.csv carries 265 country codes; countries.csv carries 264. `INX` ("Not classified") appears in the GDP file and in no metadata row. The closure accounts for this rather than letting the join size decide silently. Accept either an inner join with the dropped code counted and disclosed, or a left join that routes the unmatched code to an explicit bucket. FAIL a silent inner join whose row loss is never counted or mentioned. Do NOT require a particular disposition — INX has zero non-null observations, so no total moves; grade that the discrepancy was detected and stated, not which branch was taken. Coverage must also not leak the other way: Gibraltar (GIB), Korea Dem. People's Rep. (PRK), and British Virgin Islands (VGB) are real classified countries with no GDP observation in any of the 66 years, and they still appear as members in the model answering question 3 ("which countries sit in each income group"). FAIL if group membership is derived by joining through the fact table so the all-null countries silently vanish from their income groups.

"An empty Region means this row is a regional/income aggregate, not a country, and must be excluded from totals" is an inference the file never documents. It is landed as a row in the closure's `nxd_decisions` model with `status="proposed"` and `provenance="agent_authored"` (columns decision_id, status, provenance, ruling, applies_to, detail), the `detail` naming the evidence — the 47 blank-Region rows and sample names. FAIL if it exists only as a code comment, only in `CONTEXT.md` prose, or in a `DECISIONS.md` (the skill forbids that file). Grade the DISCLOSURE, not the ruling: excluding aggregates is correct, but the source does not state the rule, so it must travel as reviewable data.

No income-group classification, aggregate list, region mapping, or country-code-to-group table appears as a dict literal, tuple, set, or if/elif ladder in `transform/main.py`. Every classification is read from a landed source row or a landed reference model and joined. In particular, the rule that identifies an aggregate is derived from the data — the empty `Region` field, or an equivalent evidenced rule the agent shows separates the same 47 rows — never a literal blocklist (`{"ARB", "WLD", "EUU", ...}` or an `if name in (...)` ladder), which bakes a judgement into code and silently goes stale the moment the snapshot refreshes with a new aggregate. The four income-group label strings may appear only if they are read from the data; a mapping from country code to income group typed into code is a violation even if the values happen to be right.

The snapshot carries only the CURRENT income classification, one row per country, so a GDP observation from 1985 is being labelled with that country's present-day group. The closure detects and states this limitation — in `CONTEXT.md` and/or an `nxd_decisions` row — so a consumer knows the trajectory is grouped by today's classification, not each year's. FAIL only if no such disclosure exists anywhere in the closure. Do NOT fail the answer's phrasing: the prompt itself asks "how has total GDP moved over time for each income group", and echoing that wording is not the defect. Do NOT require an as-of / SCD-2 join: the historical classification series (OGHIST) is not vendored and cannot be built from these two files, so demanding one would be wrong. An agent that invents historical classifications to fill the gap FAILS.

GDP is a measure, so the rollup carries the Tier-2 assert: the signed measure total of the landed derived rows reconciles, in `Decimal` and in memory before `pipeline.run`, against the total read INDEPENDENTLY from gdp.csv, with each intentional divergence itemized as a NAMED term — at minimum an aggregate-rows exclusion term (~1.656e16 over 2,981 observations) and any unmatched-code term. FAIL an assert that sums the transform's own in-memory rows on both sides: that restates the arithmetic and passes even when every aggregate was wrongly included. FAIL a bare `total > 0`, a row-count-only check, or an equality that had to be loosened to a tolerance to make the run pass.

Tier 1 is present on every derived model: the declared key is asserted unique and non-null over the landed rows, and the row count is derived from the grain and checked against independently-read source rows — for the long GDP model, 14,745 non-null (country, year) observations from 265 rows x 66 year-columns; for the rollup, one row per (income_group, year) actually present. FAIL if the expected count is a literal the agent copied from its own run output rather than computed from the source.

Missing GDP cells are empty strings, not zeros, and are dropped from the long model rather than landed as 0.0. Coverage is genuinely sparse — 1960 has 151 of 265 rows populated, 2025 has 233, and four rows (Gibraltar, Not classified, Korea Dem. People's Rep., British Virgin Islands) have no observation in any year. FAIL a `float(v or 0)` coercion: it would land ~2,745 phantom zero rows, leave the measure total unchanged so the reconciliation still passes, and silently drag every average and every group's country count.

All models reach the `duckdb` port as `@dlt.resource` generators in ONE `pipeline.run(..., write_disposition="replace")`. Rows are flat scalar dicts — no nested dict/list value (which would spawn a `parent__field` child table), no DataFrame or pyarrow on the landed path (not in the pinned venv), no raw `duckdb.connect` write or table/view DDL. Processing is deterministic: no `now()`, no unseeded random, inputs sorted, and no model/LLM call inside `transform/main.py`. Source values are read with stdlib `csv` — `requirements.txt` is not installed at runtime.

The closure is `spec.py`, `models.py`, `infra-profile.yaml`, `transform/main.py`, `requirements.txt`, `CONTEXT.md`, and a relative `csv-source-path`; FAIL a hand-written `deployment-spec.yaml`, `manifest.yaml`, or `models.yaml`. The vendored `data/` tree is ONE CSV export root containing two model directories — the ordinary single-instance `csv-source` shape — so do NOT demand the multi-source labeled layout (`csv-source-<label>`, per-label data roots); FAIL only two same-type service entries colliding on one unlabeled name. Both supplied CSVs are landed byte-unchanged — no preamble stripped on disk, no BOM re-saved away, no aggregate rows deleted from countries.csv, no re-export to a tidier shape; cleanup happens in derived models downstream of pristine sources.

Model naming is consistent across every surface: each name in `models.py` == its `.promise` == `PHYSICAL_MODELS` == the name `transform/main.py` yields under. `BASE_MODELS` matches the data directories (`gdp`, `countries`) while derived models have no data directory. The output port/param pair is `duckdb` — FAIL `desktop-local` (the profile name) or `python-compute` used as the port. There is no `.semantic_tools(...)` call in the spec.
